epic.title: Home: the room editor, then the bathroom and the nursery
epic.description:
Phil's own web viewer in Mycelium, simple, to scale and quick to change, on the phone and the PC: rooms and walls, sized labelled boxes for furniture, two or three saved layouts per room, wall and floor colours, standing, seated, child and walk-through viewpoints. Kirsty leads the look through mood boards; Phil builds what she picks, doing nearly everything himself. One room at a time: bathroom, nursery, bedroom, living room, office. Everything moves into Mycelium; the Floorplanner FML is imported once as the fallback.

## Order
The bathroom carries on now because it is already stripped: home.12 (receipt), home.13 (moisture tests and boards), home.15 (technical record), home.14 (bath to fittings, waiting for the archived plan from rescue.01), home.16. In parallel the editor: home.01 design, home.02, home.03, home.04, with home.05 (FML), home.06 (measuring), home.07 (room plan page) and home.25, home.26 hanging off it. The nursery follows: home.09 budget and home.10 storage (before baby.07), home.11 furniture, home.08 mood boards, home.17, home.18, home.27. Then home.19 opens the next room. The learn-or-hire tickets (home.20 to home.23) are answered before the room that needs them; home.24 waits for Home Assistant (sub.08).

## Done means
The nursery is designed in the editor, bought and finished before June 2027.

## Flags
- Section 8 item 7: the editor is a build in itself and the nursery has a June date; Floorplanner as a stopgap was declined. Not reopened.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs (link filled by the integrator).

tickets.title: Editor design: a web viewer in Mycelium, to scale, boxes first, phone and PC, several layouts per room, viewpoints (standing, seated, child, walk-through); the schema with room for a second property
tickets.description:
## What
Write the design document for the room editor before any build: a page in Mycelium's new Home section that shows the house to scale, rooms first, with furniture as sized labelled boxes. Cover the data model (property, floor, room, wall, opening, item, layout, viewpoint, all in millimetres, with a property id so a second property fits later), the views (a top-down plan for placing, a 3D view for looking), the controls on a phone and on the PC, how several saved layouts per room work, the four viewpoints (standing, seated, child height, a walk-through path), and how the Floorplanner FML import (home.05) maps into the model. The dossier (dossiers/home.md, section 3.1) lists the open-source editors worth reading first (Pascal Editor on React Three Fiber, openPlan3D) and the known phone problem: the camera control and dragging a box fight over the same touch, so the design must pick one rule (for example: tap to select, then one finger moves the selected box and two fingers move the camera). Read the Next.js guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before naming any framework detail, as the repo's AGENTS.md requires.

## Why
Phil chose his own web viewer in Mycelium, simple, to scale and quick to change, working on the phone as well as the PC; the editor comes first and room decisions wait for it.

## Done looks like
A design document in claude/ (linked from claude/spec-index.md) that names the schema, the views, the touch rule, the layout and viewpoint model, the FML mapping, and the three build slices (home.02, home.03, home.04) with what each delivers. Phil has read it.

## Unlocks
home.02: slice 1 builds from this design. home.05: the FML mapping is defined here.

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Flag
Section 8 item 7: Claude flagged once that the editor is a build in itself and the nursery has a June date; Phil declined Floorplanner as a stopgap. Not reopened.

Boxes belong to a layout, so the same room can hold two or three arrangements.

## Why
Phil asked for sized, labelled boxes first and real models later, placed and moved to scale, on the phone as well as the PC.

## Done looks like
On the phone: a 1200 by 600 by 750 box can be added to the nursery, dragged against a wall, rotated, saved in one layout and absent from another. Measurements shown match the entered sizes.

tickets.title: Import the Floorplanner FML once as the fallback geometry
tickets.description:
## What
Import the corrected Floorplanner model, the only right geometry for the house, once into the editor's schema. Floorplanner describes FML as a JSON format with a published v3.0 specification (XML still supported for older files); check the file's first character to tell which. First find the exported file: it may already be in the RoomScan or Floorplanner export folder; if not, Phil exports it from his Floorplanner project. Floorplanner's own page says FML sharing comes with an upgraded project (Level 2 or a Pro account); check that the export option is offered on his project before assuming anything is bought. Keep the original file in the archive untouched; the import is one-way and becomes the fallback.

## Why
Phil decided Floorplanner's FML is imported once and becomes the fallback; it took a lot of correction effort and holds the only right geometry.

## Done looks like
The original FML file is stored in the archive, the import report lists every room with its size, and three rooms checked by hand (bathroom, smallest bedroom, office) match the Floorplanner figures within 2 cm.

## Unlocks
home.06 (the measuring round can be judged against the import).

## Depends on
home.02: the schema and room model exist.

## Cost
Exporting FML may need an upgraded Floorplanner project (paid credits). To be checked, nothing bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 44: Consumes the file home.04a stored, not a fresh export.

tickets.title: Measure the whole house: finish the laser round (decide if the Bosch is still needed), count the stair risers
tickets.description:
## What
Two short sittings in the house. First the stairs: count the risers, measure one riser height and the full rise, so the floor-to-floor height is real rather than the dollhouse viewer's placeholder. Second, decide whether the Bosch laser round is still needed: measure three rooms with the laser and compare them with the corrected Floorplanner model; within 2 cm means the round is closed.

## Why
Phil decided the whole house is measured first; the next step was counting the stair risers, and whether the Bosch round is still needed was open.

## Done looks like
The ticket's answers hold the riser count, riser height, full rise, and a yes or no on the laser round.

## Unlocks
home.02 and home.05: levels and heights are right.

## Depends on
Nothing.

steps_definition.title: Measure the whole house: the stair risers and the laser round decision

intro.answer: Count the stair risers and measure one, so the floor-to-floor height is real, and decide whether the Bosch laser round is still needed.
unlocks: home.05: the import can be checked against real heights
home.02: rooms entered at the right levels
to_hand: The Bosch laser measure (UniversalDistance 40C) or a steel tape
A pencil and the phone for photos

sources.label: Floorplanner: FML, the floorplan markup format

phases.title: Stairs: risers and one riser height

steps.title: Count the risers
steps.body_html: Count every step face from the bottom floor to the landing floor, including the last one up onto the landing. A riser is the vertical face, not the tread.
steps.expect_html: A whole number, usually 12 to 14 in a house.

steps.title: Measure one riser
steps.body_html: Measure the height of three different risers from tread top to tread top, in millimetres. Write the average.
steps.expect_html: Three figures within a few millimetres of each other.

steps.title: Measure the full rise as a check
steps.body_html: Measure from the ground floor surface to the landing floor surface with the laser held against the top nosing, or a tape down the stairwell. Compare with risers times riser height.
steps.expect_html: The two figures agree within about 10 mm. The difference is the floor finish.

steps.title: Record it
steps.body_html: Write the floor-to-floor height into the answers above. It replaces the dollhouse viewer's placeholder.

phases.title: The laser round: still needed?
needs: The Floorplanner model open on the PC

steps.title: Compare three rooms
steps.body_html: Measure the length and width of the bathroom, the smallest bedroom and the office with the laser. Compare with the Floorplanner model. The tolerance agreed earlier was 2 cm per room.
steps.expect_html: Six figures, each within 2 cm or not.

steps.title: Decide
steps.body_html: If all six are within 2 cm, the laser round is not needed: close it. If any is out, the round continues for that floor and becomes its own ticket.

tickets.title: Bathroom: insulation-board receipt mismatch resolved
tickets.description:
## What
A receipt for the bathroom boards showed the wrong insulation board. unlocks: home.13: moisture tests and board fitting

sources.label: NoMorePly 12mm fibre cement board, Toolstation listing
No More Ply 12mm wall tile backer board, Tile Mountain

steps.title: Find the receipt

steps.expect_html: A product name and code written down.

steps.title: Read the boards on site

where.label: The bathroom or where the boards are stored

tickets.title: Bathroom: moisture tests, then cut and fit the boards (diamond blade, clamped guide), boards before battens
tickets.description:
## What
Five sittings. Test the stripped brick walls with the moisture meter against a dry reference wall; only board walls that read close to it. Read the NoMorePly installation guide's fixing method for masonry. Mark every board's position (new board overlapping behind the strip the old tiles retain), then cut each 12 mm board outside with the diamond blade against a straight batten held by two clamps, and fix it with the adhesive and screws the guide names. Boards go up first; battens only after the bath is dry-fitted and level. Tanking slurry does not go on the brick first.

## Why
Phil decided the next steps after the receipt are the moisture tests, then cutting and fitting the boards with the diamond blade and a clamped guide, boards before battens.

## Done looks like
Every wall read and passed, every board on the cut list fixed and plumb.

## Unlocks
home.14 (bath, battens, tanking, tiling), home.15 (technical record while open).

## Depends on
home.12: the receipt mismatch is resolved and enough boards are in the house.

steps_definition.title: Bathroom: moisture tests, then cut and fit the boards

intro.answer: Test the bare brick is dry, then cut each 12 mm board with the diamond blade against a clamped guide and fix it, boards before battens.
unlocks: home.15: the technical record while the walls are open
to_hand: Angle grinder or saw with the diamond blade
Adhesive and fibre cement screws named in that guide
time: About 1 hour 15 minutes over five sittings

sources.label: NoMorePly 12mm fibre cement board, Toolstation listing
No More Ply 12mm wall tile backer board, Tile Mountain
No More Ply installation guide (PDF, Pure Adhesion)
HSE construction dust FAQ (FFP3 for silica work)
HSE construction dust: scabbling or grinding (extraction plus RPE)
Tiling guide page citing BS 5385 on wet-area substrates (Tile Association)

hard_part.why: One straight cut decides whether the board fits; two boards were already lost to a knife.

steps.title: Set the meter
steps.body_html: Set the meter to its masonry (or brick) mode. Take one reading on a wall in a dry room as your reference.

steps.title: Read each wall
steps.body_html: On each stripped wall take readings at about 150 mm, 1 m and 1.8 m high, near corners and near the old bath line. Write the highest per wall.

steps.title: Pass or wait
steps.body_html: If any wall reads clearly above the dry reference, wait a week with the room ventilated and test again. Damp brick is not boarded. Look for a cause (a leak, a cold bridge) if it does not fall.

fields.label: All walls close to the reference?

notes.html: No published pass mark for brick before boarding was found; the meter maker's chart and the dry reference are the guide. The dossier says so.

phases.title: Read the guide and set out

steps.title: Read the fixing method
steps.body_html: Read how the guide fixes 12 mm boards to masonry (adhesive, screws per board, joints) and which tape and tanking it requires in a shower zone. Write the method.
steps.expect_html: A written method: adhesive, screw count and length, joint treatment.

notes.html: The lifetime guarantee depends on following that guide and using its named essentials.

steps.title: Mark the board positions
steps.body_html: Draw where each board goes on each wall, with the new board overlapping behind the strip retained by the old tiles, and joints away from the corner of the bath where possible.
steps.expect_html: Every board drawn on the wall with its size.

steps.title: Cut list
steps.body_html: Write each cut: board number, width, height.

steps.title: Measure and mark
steps.body_html: Mark the cut on the face of the board, measured twice.

steps.title: Clamp the guide
steps.body_html: Clamp the straight batten along the line with two clamps, set so the blade's edge runs on the waste side.
steps.expect_html: The guide does not move when pushed.

steps.title: Cut
steps.body_html: Cut along the guide with the diamond blade in one steady pass.
steps.expect_html: A straight edge within a millimetre or two of the line.

notes.html: Fibre cement contains crystalline silica. Cut outside, with on-tool extraction if the saw has it, and wear an FFP3 mask (HSE's advice for silica dust). Eye protection too.

troubleshooting.fix: Slow down and support the off-cut so it does not drop at the end.

steps.title: Dry fit
steps.body_html: Hold the board in place. Check the fit against the overlap and the bath line.
steps.expect_html: The board sits flat with the gaps the guide asks for.

steps.title: Adhesive
steps.body_html: Apply the adhesive the guide names, in the pattern it gives.

steps.title: Press and screw
steps.body_html: Press the board on, check it is plumb, and fix the screws the guide names (it gives about 9 per board for this size) so the board cannot move while the adhesive cures.

steps.title: Clean up
steps.body_html: Wipe off squeezed-out adhesive and note the board as done on the cut list.

phases.title: The remaining boards, one per sitting

steps.title: Repeat phases 3 and 4 per board
steps.body_html: One board per sitting: mark, clamp, cut, dry fit, fix. Record each board on the cut list. Battens go on only after the bath is dry-fitted and level (home.14).
steps.expect_html: All boards on the cut list ticked.

notes.html: Fibre cement contains crystalline silica. Cut outside, with on-tool extraction if the saw has it, and wear an FFP3 mask (HSE's advice for silica dust). Eye protection too.

tickets.title: Bathroom: the existing plan and shopping list as tickets; the 1700 P-shaped bath fitted
tickets.description:
## What
One ticket with a phase per known step, because the detailed bathroom plan is not in the repo. The plan, shopping list and job checklist were made in Claude chats and artifacts and come in through rescue.01 (phase 1 opens them; the ticket waits if they are missing). Then: the Nuie Ceramica 1700 P-shaped left-hand shower bath with reinforced base is dry-fitted and levelled on the concrete floor, battens fitted, the bath lifted out, the boards taped and tanked in two coats, the bath fixed with the click-clack waste and water-tested, the walls tiled one per sitting (or by a tiler if home.21 says hire), then the thermostatic deck-mounted mixer, panel, screen and silicone.

## Why
The bathroom is folded fully into this epic: its existing plan and shopping list become tickets here, and the wider bath is so Kirsty can be in the bath with the baby comfortably.

## Done looks like
The bath is fitted, the walls tiled, the mixer working with no drips, the silicone sealed; the shopping list fully ticked.

## Unlocks
home.16: the before-and-after page.

## Depends on
home.13: boards fitted. rescue.01: the archived plan, shopping list and job checklist. home.21: tiling decided.

## Red team
- Finding 25: The bathroom's budget is the first row of home.09; items above it wait.

steps.body_html: Tape every board joint and internal corner with the kit's tape, as its instructions say. Tanking goes on the boards, not the brick.

steps.title: First coat
steps.body_html: Apply the first coat over the shower and bath zone as the kit says. Leave to dry for the time the kit gives.

steps.title: Second coat
steps.body_html: Apply the second coat at right angles to the first. Leave to cure as the kit says before tiling.

steps.title: Record the cure time
steps.body_html: Write the date and time tiling can start.

phases.title: Bath fixed and sealed to the wall

steps.title: Fix the bath
steps.body_html: Set the bath back, level it, connect the click-clack waste, and fix it as its instructions say.

steps.title: Fill and test
steps.body_html: Fill the bath with water before sealing (so it settles) and check the waste for drips.

steps.title: Learn it or hire it
steps.body_html: If home.21 decided to hire a tiler, book them and skip to phase 8.

steps.title: Tile one wall
steps.body_html: Tile one wall per sitting from a level batten line. Record each wall done.

steps.title: Deck-mounted mixer
steps.body_html: Fit the thermostatic deck-mounted mixer with the pipes through the existing wall cavity, as its instructions say.

steps.title: Panel and screen
steps.body_html: Fit the bath panel and the shower screen.

steps.title: Seal
steps.body_html: With the bath full, run silicone along the bath and tile joint.

## What

Small patches (office.05, the render in repairs.03) are a good practice piece before a whole wall. Write the decision and, if learning, the one guide or course to follow.

tickets.title: Learn it or hire it: electrical work beyond swapping fittings
tickets.description:
## What
Decide, before the room that needs it, whether Phil learns electrical work beyond swapping fittings himself or hires someone. Look at: the area involved, a practice piece first (an off-cut or a wall nobody sees), the cost of a tradesperson's quote against tools and materials, and the time. In England, a new circuit, a new consumer unit, or adding to a circuit in the zone around a bath or shower is notifiable under Part P: done by a registered electrician who certifies it, or notified to building control before work starts (which costs a fee). Like-for-like fitting swaps are not notifiable. Sources: dossiers/home.md, section 3.6. Write the decision and, if learning, the one guide or course to follow.

## Why
Phil does nearly everything himself, and each job he has not done before gets a 'learn it or hire it' ticket.
